methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $20M total raised proxy.

data.narrative:
Amperon is a Series B infrastructure and logistics company founded by Sean Kelly that has raised $20M to date. The valuation analysis is constrained by the absence of comparable public equities and identified private peers in the infrastructure and logistics sector, limiting triangulation to stage-progression methodology alone.

The stage-progression method applies a 1.9x multiplier to the $20M total capital raised as a proxy for current value, yielding an implied valuation of $38M. This multiplier reflects typical venture step-ups observed in Series B to subsequent-stage transitions. The analysis supports a range of $32M (low) to $44M (high), with $38M as the median point. The relatively narrow band reflects confidence in the stage-progression input but also the methodological constraint of relying on a single approach.

Key uncertainties include the lack of sector-specific comparable companies to validate the 1.9x multiplier against actual Infrastructure & Logistics precedents, and the absence of visibility into Amperon's unit economics, revenue trajectory, or capital efficiency relative to peer benchmarks. A fuller valuation would benefit from either identifying relevant private or public comparables or incorporating revenue multiple analysis if operational metrics become available. Current range: $32M–$44M.
